title: Contentment with what comes
literal_meaning: In food there is no good or bad: whatever is available in a place.
explanation: The verse sets aside distinctions between preferred and less preferred food: one accepts what is available. A related passage in Jagannath Das’s Odia Bhagabata places this thought in the Avadhuta’s account to King Yadu of equanimity and the python as a teacher. Read in everyday conversation, it can counsel contentment instead of constant complaint. That everyday application is an interpretation, not an account of the saying’s first use.
meaning_odia: ଯେଉଁଠି ଯାହା ମିଳେ, ତାହାକୁ ସନ୍ତୋଷରେ ଗ୍ରହଣ କରିବାର କଥା ଏହି ପଦରେ ଅଛି। ଜଗନ୍ନାଥ ଦାସଙ୍କ ଭାଗବତର ଏକ ସମ୍ପର୍କିତ ପାଠରେ ଅବଧୂତ ଯଦୁ ରାଜାଙ୍କୁ ନିଜର ସମଭାବ ଓ ଅଜଗରଠାରୁ ଶିଖିଥିବା ଧର୍ମ ବିଷୟରେ କହନ୍ତି। ସେଠାରେ ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଅଳ୍ପ ବା ବହୁତ ହେଲେ ବି ସନ୍ତୋଷ ରହେ। ଦୈନନ୍ଦିନ କଥାରେ ପଦଟି ଅନାବଶ୍ୟକ ଖୁଣ ନ ଧରି, ମିଳିଥିବା ଜିନିଷକୁ ନେଇ ଚଳିବାର ପରାମର୍ଶ ହୋଇପାରେ।
usage_example: On a visit, a guest welcomes a simple meal instead of complaining that a favourite dish is missing. (Original imagined occasion.)
cultural_context: The related Bhagabata text is an ascetic teaching about contentment. Its chapter 9, verse 5 reads ଯେମନ୍ତ where the selected Incubator witness reads ଯେବଣ; keep both readings distinct. Neither this comparison nor the modern compilation establishes a first coinage or a direction of borrowing.
odia_summary: ଯେଉଁଠି ଯାହା ମିଳେ, ତାହାକୁ ନେଇ ସନ୍ତୋଷରେ ଚଳିବାର କଥା।
english_summary: Contentment with what is available, instead of constantly measuring it against preference.
